definitions.gloss: tough; formidable; hard to beat; hard to deal with
definitions.explanation: Describes an opponent, task, or situation that is difficult to overcome. Implies that the difficulty comes from the strength or skill of the opposition, not just the complexity of the task.

examples.japanese: {今回|こんかい}の{試験|しけん}は{手|て}ごわかった。
{交渉|こうしょう}{相手|あいて}がなかなか{手|て}ごわくて、{話|はなし}がまとまらない。
examples.english: The other party in the negotiation is quite tough, and we can't reach an agreement.

notes: Also written as {手強|てごわ}い. Literally 'hard on the hands,' suggesting something that resists your efforts. Commonly used in sports ({手|て}ごわい{相手|あいて}, tough opponent), business ({手|て}ごわい{交渉|こうしょう}, tough negotiation), and games. The opposite is {手|て}ぬるい (lenient, too easy on). Distinguished from {難|むずか}しい (difficult in general) — {手|て}ごわい specifically implies resistance or opposition that makes something hard to overcome.
